name: Mongol Sack of Kiev
summary: Batu Khan's western Mongol army, guided by Subutai, storms Kiev after a brief siege in December 1240. Contemporary accounts describe the city reduced to rubble; a Franciscan friar passing through in 1246 found only a few hundred houses standing and skulls piled in fields. The metropolitan see flees north to Vladimir and eventually Moscow. The Kievan political system, a loose confederation of Rus' principalities, ceases to exist as an independent entity.

_quarry.structural_significance: Ends Kievan Rus as a political entity and shifts the center of Russian civilization northward to Vladimir-Suzdal and eventually Moscow; the Golden Horde's 'Tatar Yoke' subjects Russian princes to tribute payments for 240 years; the population and economic collapse retards Russian development relative to Western Europe
